cards.explanation: The answer is False. Verse 9 says the Teacher "…also taught the people knowledge…" (Ecclesiastes 12:9). The Teacher was king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1), and the wisdom went out to the people. Keeping it all to himself doesn't match that, friends.

The answer is accurate and true. The text says he searched "…to record accurate words of truth." (Ecclesiastes 12:10). He went looking for delightful sayings, and he wanted what he wrote down to be right. A pretty saying that's off is like a cookie that looks great and has no sugar in it.

The answer is nails, friends. "…the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails…" (Ecclesiastes 12:11). I've been pulled out of a drawer, but a firmly embedded nail? That thing isn't going anywhere. I've never been that committed to a spot in my life, and I live on a gold base.

The answer is driven in deep. They're "…firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd." (Ecclesiastes 12:11). Firmly embedded means they're in there and they're staying. I've been stuck in a drawer, so I can tell you that stuck and secure are different things, bakers.

The answer is True, friends. The warning says, "There is no end to the making of many books…" (Ecclesiastes 12:12). Books keep on coming. My cookie recipe pile is already out of hand, and I only have one bakery.

The answer is wearies. The warning says, "…much study wearies the body." (Ecclesiastes 12:12). Anybody who has read for hours and then lost the will to stand up knows this one. Even good things can wear a body out. Time to stretch, friends.

The answer is whole, friends. "Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man." (Ecclesiastes 12:13). Whole, as in all of it. The verse opens with "When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this…" So after everything the Teacher has said, this is where it lands.

The answer is the good and the evil ones, bakers. God will bring every deed into judgment, "…along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil." (Ecclesiastes 12:14). Both kinds are covered, the good and the evil. Nothing hidden gets left out.
